sentences.text: Ampelosaurus is the only known species of its genus, representing a moderate-sized titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
This animal possessed a long neck and tail typical of sauropods and was covered in armor made of osteoderms ranging from 25 to 28 centimeters in length.

The holotype specimen consists of three connected dorsal vertebrae, while other distinguishing features include weakly spatulate teeth, laterally widening neural spine extremities, and a scapula measuring 72 centimeters in length.
The name Ampelosaurus means "vineyard lizard," a reference to the Blanquette de Limoux vineyard where the species was first described by Jean Le Loeuff in 1995.
Fossil evidence of dinosaur eggshells and nests has been found in the same rock layers where Ampelosaurus fossils occur.
Fossils of Ampelosaurus atacis have been discovered at the Upper Cretaceous Bellevue locality in southern France, specifically at the base of the Marnes de la Maurine Member in the Upper Aude Valley.
Over 500 bones discovered since 1989 at this locality have been assigned to Ampelosaurus atacis.
Reports of Ampelosaurus remains in the Petites Pyrénées and Chaînon de Saint-Chinian have never been confirmed by a formal publication.

Ampelosaurus exhibited a slower growth rate after its bone microstructure became unique among sauropods, and the onset of growth was clearly delayed compared to other sauropods where it typically starts around sexual maturity.

No growth marks have been found on any bone samples of Ampelosaurus, and the animal has not been found to possess EFS, a feature common in most non-titanosaurian sauropods. Most specimens show secondary osteons densely placed in the inner bone regions and lightly in the outer regions, and no medullary cavity has been found in any bones.
Researchers suggest that Ampelosaurus might have had EFS because larger specimens were not tested in the study that reported its absence.
Ampelosaurus is the sister taxon to Atsinganosaurus, and their shared clade is positioned phylogenetically between Saltasauridae and the groups Aeolosaurini or Lognkosauria.
Ampelosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous Period, specifically the Early Maastrichtian epoch, approximately 71.5 million years ago.
Ampelosaurus remains were recovered from the lower levels of the Marnes Rouges Inférieures Formation, dating to approximately 70 million years ago.

A 2012 study suggested that Bellevue contained three morphotypes of titanosaurs, with one tentatively assigned to the genus Lirainosaurus, creating debate over species attribution. Researchers in 2021 agreed that a second titanosaur species existed at Bellevue but suggested it was more similar to the genus Garrigatitan. Recent studies indicate that the diagnosis of Ampelosaurus will need to be revised due to the presence of additional titanosaur species at the site. Recent studies suggest that many bones previously assigned to Ampelosaurus belong to a distinct species, potentially requiring the description of a new titanosaur and an emended diagnosis for Ampelosaurus. It is debated whether there were at least two different titanosaurs in southern France during the Late Cretaceous, as another skull showed some differences.
